You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE museum (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Num_of_Staff INT,
    Open_Year TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visitor (
    ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Level_of_membership INT,
    Age INT,
    UNIQUE (ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visit (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    visitor_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Num_of_Ticket INT,
    Total_spent REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (visitor_ID) REFERENCES visitor(ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Museum_ID) REFERENCES museum(Museum_ID)
);

To list **frequent museum visitors**, we need to define “frequent” (e.g., *number of visits* ≥ N, or *top K* visitors by visit count). Here are common options.

### 1) Top 10 most frequent visitors (by number of visits)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
ORDER BY num_visits DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

### 2) Visitors with at least 5 visits (set your threshold)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY num_visits DESC;
```

### 3) Frequent per museum (top 3 visitors for each museum)
```sql
SELECT
  m.Museum_ID,
  m.Name AS museum_name,
  v.ID AS visitor_id,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits
FROM museum m
JOIN visit vi ON vi.Museum_ID = m.Museum_ID
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
GROUP BY m.Museum_ID, m.Name, v.ID, v.Name
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
  PARTITION BY m.Museum_ID
  ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
) <= 3;
```

Which definition do you want: **top N overall**, **at least X visits**, or **top per museum**? Also, what threshold (N or X)?
consider only those who have gone to these museums

Which museums are “these museums” (a list of `Museum_ID`s or names)?  

Here are two templates depending on what you mean:

### A) Visitors who have visited **any** of the specified museums
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits_to_list
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
WHERE vi.Museum_ID IN (/* museum ids, e.g. 1,2,3 */)
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
ORDER BY num_visits_to_list DESC;
```

### B) Visitors who have visited **all** of the specified museums
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) AS museums_visited_in_list
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
WHERE vi.Museum_ID IN (/* museum ids, e.g. 1,2,3 */)
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) = (
  SELECT COUNT(*)
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT Museum_ID
        FROM museum
        WHERE Museum_ID IN (/* same list */)) x
);
```

Send the museum list and whether you want **any** vs **all**, and I’ll plug it in (and add a “frequent” threshold if needed).
I want to look for visitors who have been to museums multiple times.

If “multiple times” means **more than 1 visit total**, use:

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY num_visits DESC;
```

If instead you mean **multiple times to the same museum** (repeat visits per museum):

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  vi.Museum_ID,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits_to_museum
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, vi.Museum_ID
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY num_visits_to_museum DESC, v.ID;
```
Just need to get the unique IDs of these visitors.

For visitors who have visited **multiple times (overall)** and you only want unique IDs:

```sql
SELECT vi.visitor_ID
FROM visit vi
GROUP BY vi.visitor_ID
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```

If you meant multiple times **to the same museum**:

```sql
SELECT vi.visitor_ID
FROM visit vi
GROUP BY vi.visitor_ID, vi.Museum_ID
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```
just need the visitor names with those IDs too

For visitors who visited **multiple times overall**, return unique ID + name:

```sql
SELECT v.ID, v.Name
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```

If you meant multiple times **to the same museum**, use:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT v.ID, v.Name
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, vi.Museum_ID
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```
don't forget to focus on visitors to museums specifically

To focus only on **visitors who have museum visits recorded** and who visited **more than once**, use an inner join to `visit`:

```sql
SELECT v.ID, v.Name
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```
Also, I need to get the ages of these visitors along with their names.

```sql
SELECT v.ID, v.Name, v.Age
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Age
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```
